$comment: AUTHORED source for registry.json. Prose and identity live here; `files`, `dependencies` and `registryDependencies` are DERIVED from the block source by `pnpm gen` — never hand-write them. See .claude/rules/registry.md.
name: brand-ui

items.name: app-shell
items.title: App shell
items.description: Sidebar + top nav + page layout scaffold for an internal app.

items.name: ai-chat-shell
items.title: AI chat shell
items.description: Chat surface with transcript, composer, tool calls and a context rail.

items.name: data-table
items.title: Data table
items.description: Filterable, sortable, paginated TanStack data table with toolbar.

items.name: chart-frame-data
items.title: ChartFrame + data table
items.description: ChartFrame (expand / flip-to-table / download-CSV) wired to @elabs-ai/components-data: full TanStack DataTable on flip and downloadCsv on export.

items.name: ai-chart
items.title: AI chart in conversation
items.description: Renders a model's chart tool-output inside an AI conversation — AutoChart (@elabs-ai/components-charts) composed with Tool/ToolOutput from @elabs-ai/components-ai. The canonical copy-owned home for @elabs-ai/components-ai + @elabs-ai/components-charts cross-sibling composition.

items.name: flow-canvas
items.title: Flow canvas
items.description: Branded React Flow canvas with custom nodes, edges and controls.

items.name: flow-builder
items.title: Flow builder
items.description: Workflow-builder canvas with a node palette, auto-layout, grouping, placeholder growth, insert-between, an inspector, and copy-own undo/redo + copy/paste.

items.name: marketing-hero
items.title: Marketing hero
items.description: Landing hero section with eyebrow, headline, CTAs and logo strip.

items.name: code-workspace
items.title: Code workspace
items.description: Multi-file Monaco code editor with brand-ui tabs and token theming (wire @elabs-ai/components-editor/monaco-environment once at the app entry).
items.$comment-extraDependencies: A third-party PEER of a dependency that this block genuinely needs at runtime. Brand (@elabs-ai/*) peers are added automatically; a third-party peer is conditional on what the block renders, so it is declared. @elabs-ai/components-editor owns globalThis.MonacoEnvironment and cannot render without monaco-editor installed.

items.name: sidebar-02
items.title: App shell — dashboard inset
items.description: The classic left-sidebar dashboard: a collapsible-icon nav rail with a tenant switcher and nav groups beside a floating inset surface carrying a metric row, a revenue trend and an overnight activity feed. Skip link, one main landmark, active-route indicator and command trigger included.

items.name: sidebar-04
items.title: App shell — mail
items.description: Three-zone mail shell: the collapsible icon rail, a searchable message list, and a reading pane sharing one floating inset surface. A variation on the dashboard shell, not a separate idea; below md the two content zones become a drill-down.

items.name: sidebar-05
items.title: App shell — dual rail
items.description: Two navigation levels plus a summoned third surface: a permanent 56px icon rail picks the area, a collapsible second panel lists that area's sections, and the floating inset carries the settings screen. A resizable right-hand SideDock holds the change history — a column above 1100px, an overlay below it. The icon rail is deliberately not a Sidebar, so it survives every breakpoint while the section panel becomes a sheet.

items.name: stat-card-parts
items.title: Stat Card — shared parts
items.description: The pieces every stat-card block shares: the edge-to-edge chart bleed wrapper, the chart-hover→value/label/trend bridge, and the tokenized trend badge. Installed once and reused by the stat-card blocks rather than copied into each.

items.name: stat-card-area-01
items.title: Stat Card — Area
items.description: KPI stat card with a live area chart sparkline, hover-driven value/label updates, and a tokenized trend badge.

items.name: stat-card-line-01
items.title: Stat Card — Line
items.description: KPI stat card with an inline line chart, hover-driven value/label updates, and a tokenized trend badge.

items.name: stat-card-choropleth-01
items.title: Stat Card — Choropleth Map
items.description: KPI stat card with a choropleth world-map chart, hover-driven country value/label updates, and a tokenized trend badge.

items.name: stat-cards-01
items.title: Stat Cards — elevated KPI tiles
items.description: Elevated KPI tiles beyond a flat number: MetricCard + inline Sparkline (bar or line, coloured by a --chart-* token), a goal/progress tile, and a this-vs-last comparison tile.

items.name: chart-card-kpi-01
items.title: Chart Card — KPI header
items.description: An elevated chart-in-a-card: a header with a headline KPI + delta + a segmented period control (ToggleGroup), a token-coloured AreaChart, and a footer breakdown legend. The period control re-renders the chart.

items.name: stat-list-01
items.title: Stat List — ranked list, leaderboard, activity feed
items.description: Compact summary widgets: a ranked list with share bars + delta (Sales by country), a leaderboard (Top performers), and a transaction/activity feed with signed amounts.

items.name: integration-grid-01
items.title: Integration Grid
items.description: A responsive grid of integration cards (icon + name + description + connect/manage action + connection status) under a page header with an Add action — the canonical ‘connect your tools’ surface. Logos are consumer-supplied (Lucide placeholders here).

items.name: form-wizard-01
items.title: Form Wizard — checkout flow
items.description: A multi-step form with a horizontal numbered stepper (the Wizard primitive) — a checkout flow (Customer → Shipping → Payment → Review) with real fields, correct autocomplete/type hints, and a Descriptions review step.

items.name: terminal-session-idle
items.title: Terminal session (idle)
items.description: A settled coding-agent console: launch banner, transcript, composer with mode/effort indicator, status bar. Nothing is running.

items.name: terminal-session-mid-turn
items.title: Terminal session (mid-turn)
items.description: A coding-agent console under way: tool calls, a diff hunk, a working line with a stop affordance, a pending permission prompt, status bar.

items.name: chart-editorial-hourglass
items.title: Chart Editorial — Hourglass Stream
items.description: A funnel redrawn as counted barcode strips (UnitStack) with trickle threads (DrawPath) narrowing between stages, plus stage-to-stage conversion callouts. One-off editorial composition adapted from lieflat-charts' 'L13 Hourglass Stream', built entirely from @elabs-ai/components-charts' marks layer.

items.name: chart-editorial-patchwork
items.title: Chart Editorial — Radial Patchwork
items.description: Events on a 24 h clock face, density shown by overlaid translucent sectors (fill-opacity 0.07–0.16 — the one sanctioned use of transparency in this system) with rim ticks and a category legend. One-off editorial composition adapted from lieflat-charts' 'L10 Radial Patchwork'.

items.name: chart-editorial-almanac
items.title: Chart Editorial — Bubble Almanac
items.description: A category × category matrix drawn as hand-irregular blob bubbles on ruled ledger paper, with a margin note calling out the busiest cell (PeakRing + Marginalia). One-off editorial composition adapted from lieflat-charts' 'L9 Bubble Almanac'.

items.name: process-explorer-page
items.title: Process explorer page
items.description: The process-explorer archetype: KPI strip, filter bar, a process map with its accessible table twin, a variant rail, and a case table opening a single case's timeline in a bottom sheet — all driven by one useProcessExplorer instance so no two panels can disagree.

items.name: kpi-card-parts
items.title: KPI Card — shared parts
items.description: The pieces every KPI card block shares: a named-baseline comparison row (delta + arrow + sign, pp vs % handled explicitly), an on-track/at-risk/off-track status (icon + text, never colour alone), an as-of freshness footnote, Intl.* value/delta formatters, and the shared fictional 'Acme Logistics' Q3 dataset every block reads from. Installed once and reused by the KPI card blocks rather than copied into each.

items.name: kpi-target-bullet-01
items.title: KPI Cards — On target?
items.description: "Am I on target?" — a grid of KPI cards, each a BulletChart (value against target, last year, and 2–3 qualitative bands) plus a named comparison row and an as-of footnote. A lower-is-better KPI states that its bands read best-to-worst in reverse.

items.name: kpi-multi-baseline-01
items.title: KPI Cards — Compared to what?
items.description: "Compared to what?" — one wide card per KPI stacking three named baselines (target, last year, budget), each with a shared-scale dot strip so the same number's distance to every reference reads at a glance.

items.name: kpi-pace-01
items.title: KPI Cards — On pace?
items.description: "Will I make it by period end?" — quarter-to-date Progress bars with a marker for the expected pace and a computed days-ahead/behind status, plus a Gauge card reading a rate KPI against its target and thresholds.

items.name: kpi-trend-reference-01
items.title: KPI Cards — Better or worse than normal?
items.description: "Better or worse than normal?" — a 13-week Sparkline trend read against a target pace, last year, and a normal operating band, with a text legend spelling out the line styles so the encoding never rides on colour alone.

items.name: infographic-scorecard-01
items.title: Infographic Scorecard
items.description: The Power BI-style scorecard, done with an honest baseline on every number: one row per KPI — actual, target, a signed delta, a BulletChart progress-to-target, a 13-week trend, and a named status — in a horizontally scrollable Table.

items.name: kpi-forecast-01
items.title: KPI Cards — Where will I land?
items.description: "Where will I land?" — a linear run-rate projection to the end of the quarter: solid actual, dashed projection, a ±1σ confidence range that widens toward period end, a labelled target line and a today marker separating the two, with the projection method stated in words.

items.name: kpi-hero-satellites-01
items.title: KPI Cards — What is the headline?
items.description: "What is the headline?" — one hero KPI (a big value, a named comparison vs target, a 13-week trend against last year) with three compact satellite KPIs beside it, each a value + signed delta vs target + a tiny trend, composed as one card with a single separation gesture.

items.name: kpi-composition-01
items.title: KPI Cards — What is it made of?
items.description: "What is it made of?" — a 100%-stacked segmented bar per card (revenue by channel, shipments by region) plus a legend list that is the accessible source of truth: label, share, absolute value, and the share's own change vs last year in pp. Bar and legend share one order and a rank number so colour is never the only link between a segment and its row; shares under 3% merge into "Other".

items.name: kpi-ratio-unit-01
items.title: KPI Cards — How big is it?
items.description: "How big is it in human terms?" — a rate restated as a small, countable fraction ("1 in 12 orders arrived late") via UnitChart, with the exact rate spelled out beneath the rounded headline and a comparison vs last year. Highlighted units use an accent fill against a neutral rest rather than hue alone.

items.name: kpi-movers-01
items.title: KPI Cards — What changed most?
items.description: "What changed most?" — the top 3 risers and top 3 fallers in a ranked depot field (on-time delivery, revenue), each row stating its rank, how many places it moved, and a diverging mini bar from a shared, stated zero axis. Distinct from stat-list-01's single-snapshot share bars: this is about movement between two points in time.

items.name: kpi-distribution-01
items.title: KPI Cards — Is it consistent?
items.description: "Is it consistent?" — an average hides the tail: a median headline next to p90/p95 read against a named SLA threshold, a box plot of the record-level distribution with the threshold drawn as a reference line, and the share past it stated in text.

items.name: kpi-streak-01
items.title: KPI Cards — How reliable is it?
items.description: "How reliable is it?" — a ratio/streak headline over a 30-day strip of day cells, missed days marked by shape as well as colour, with the current and longest streaks and a comparison to the prior 30 days.

items.name: infographic-variance-bridge-01
items.title: Infographic — What drove the change?
items.description: "What drove the change?" — a revenue bridge from last quarter's total to this quarter's, split into price, volume, mix, FX and other, built with WaterfallChart and a Leader callout on the one or two steps that actually explain the move. Steps sum exactly to the ending total; every step states its own sign in words, never colour alone.

items.name: infographic-annotated-trend-01
items.title: Infographic — What happened, and when?
items.description: "What happened, and when?" — a 20-week LineChart with up to three labelled events anchored to the exact data point they explain, connected by a Leader, never a legend. Compact keeps only the most consequential event.

items.name: kpi-status-threshold-01
items.title: KPI Cards — Should I act?
items.description: "Should I act?" — a status (icon + text, never colour alone) read against a visible on-track/at-risk/off-track threshold scale with today's value marked, plus how long the current status has held.

items.name: infographic-cohort-retention-01
items.title: Infographic — Do customers stay?
items.description: "Do customers stay?" — a triangular cohort retention heatmap: one row per monthly signup cohort, one column per month since signup, shaded by the share still active. A cohort younger than N months draws an empty cell, never a fabricated zero. One cohort is called out with a peak ring and a stated, computed gap against its named peers.

items.name: infographic-part-to-whole-01
items.title: Infographic — Where does the money go?
items.description: "Where does the money go?" — a two-level treemap of Q3 cost, category → sub-category, drawn in one neutral mono shade except for the single highlighted tile, outlined and named with a Leader + HaloText callout stating its share and the change from last quarter. Tile area is exactly proportional to cost.

items.name: infographic-small-multiples-01
items.title: Infographic — Which depot is the outlier?
items.description: "Which depot is the outlier?" — twelve depots, one tiny 13-week line per tile, every tile on the same shared y-axis so height compares directly, with the one depot that stands out ringed and coloured (PeakRing) while every other depot stays on a muted neutral.

items.name: infographic-before-after-01
items.title: Infographic — Who improved, who slipped?
items.description: "Who improved, who slipped?" — a DumbbellChart slope chart of 6 depots, Q2 → Q3, with the biggest riser and biggest faller emphasised and every other depot on a shared muted line; direction is carried by the line's own slope, never colour alone.

items.name: infographic-gap-to-benchmark-01
items.title: Infographic — How far from the benchmark?
items.description: "How far from the benchmark?" — a sorted DumbbellChart, one row per depot, hollow benchmark marker vs filled actual marker, worst gap first, with the widest gaps emphasised; the gap's sign correctly flips for a lower-is-better metric.

items.name: dashboard-tile-table
items.title: Dashboard tile — table
items.description: A DashboardTileKind wrapping @elabs-ai/components-data's DataTable: selection tri-state dims/frames excluded rows, a row click toggles that row's field value into the sheet's selection.

items.name: dashboard-tile-chat
items.title: Dashboard tile — chat
items.description: A DashboardTileKind wrapping @elabs-ai/components-ai's ChatShell/Composer: the composer is disabled when the sheet's interactions.active is false.

items.name: dashboard-tile-process-map
items.title: Dashboard tile — process map
items.description: A DashboardTileKind wrapping @elabs-ai/components-process's ProcessMap: the sheet's tri-state selection maps 1:1 onto ProcessMap's own selectionStates, and a node click emits that activity as the tile's selection.

items.name: dashboard-sheet-app
items.title: Dashboard sheet app
items.description: The installable canonical full-screen, user-editable dashboard: app nav + DashboardToolbar + DashboardSelectionBar + asset/properties panels + DashboardSheet, with the table/chat/process-map tile blocks registered alongside the built-in kinds.

items.name: agent-ops-parts
items.title: Agent Ops — shared parts
items.description: The pieces every agent-ops block shares: a provenance line (source · freshness) for any figure, a word-sized confidence meter, an evidence chip (the kind of document a derivation read), a countable evidence-strength meter ("|||| 4 of 5"), an actor avatar that tells copilot / agent / person apart by glyph, Intl.* money/count/relative-time formatters, and the shared fictional "Atlas" AI-ops dataset (Acme Logistics) every block reads from. Installed once and reused by the agent-ops blocks rather than copied into each.

items.name: kpi-provenance-strip-01
items.title: KPI Cards — Where does this number come from?
items.description: "Where the business stands" — four headline figures on ONE surface, each with an inline signed delta and the line that earns the number its place: source and freshness ("ERP · 2 min ago", "Derived from 61 open orders · 06:02"). Peers separated by hairlines, no value without provenance; the delta is secondary (arrow + sign, never colour alone).

items.name: insight-feed-01
items.title: Insight Feed — What changed while you were away?
items.description: The AI-ops briefing pattern: a numbered feed of things the copilot did or noticed — a one-sentence fact, a paragraph of why, the evidence it read, its confidence and two actions — with a conflict item that carries no confidence ("No verdict — a person decides"). Beside it, a "Needs a person" rail of what stopped and a "Derivation load" split of applied / sent to you / pinned by people.

items.name: provenance-record-01
items.title: Provenance Record — Where did each field come from?
items.description: A record whose every field says where its value came from: derived (confidence meter + evidence kind), pinned (who and when — a pin out-ranks any derivation), conflict (two permitted sources disagree; nothing chosen) or empty ("No signal yet" — never a guess). Each state has its own glyph + text, and the footer counts the four so the reader knows how much of the record is machine-derived.

items.name: score-explanation-01
items.title: Score Explanation — Why is the score 91?
items.description: A scored decision decomposed into its signals: one row per signal, a signed bar whose length is the contribution in points and whose direction is the sign — ink for positive, the warning rung for negative, each with a signed number so the sign never rides on colour. One shared zero-based scale; the footer states how many weaker signals were considered but not shown.

items.name: spend-against-limit-01
items.title: Spend Against Limit — How close is each agent to its ceiling?
items.description: Every non-human spender on the card programme, sorted by share of ceiling: monospace agent id, autonomy band as a status badge (Auto / Review / Hold), a bar with the ceiling drawn as a vertical mark, the literal "$612 of $500", and Revoke. Over the ceiling paints the destructive rung and says so. Above it, three autonomy-band tiles total the envelopes per band.

items.name: escalation-boundary-01
items.title: Escalation Boundary — Where does autonomy end?
items.description: The one dial an AI-ops product must put on screen: a stacked distribution bar of every decision by how well it was corroborated, with the evidence threshold drawn as a mark; the evidence ladder (countable tick meter, meaning, decisions, share, side); and three "If you move it" scenario cards that state the trade in the reader’s units (cleared share, queue delta, catches, reviews per catch) and MOVE the boundary when clicked.

items.name: decision-record-01
items.title: Decision Record — Why did the AI do that?
items.description: Every AI action expanded into the reason it happened: what it did, what it looked at (named, openable evidence), what rule applied (the clause, monospace), how confident (or an honest "not applicable"), and how to reverse it. Below: the check list (confirmed / not confirmed) and what the copilot proposes — numbered, editable, nothing actioned until a person approves.

items.name: audit-log-01
items.title: Audit Log — Who did what, and did it apply?
items.description: An append-only audit table whose actor column tells three authors apart by glyph — copilot, delegated agent, person — and whose result column is a status badge with an icon (Applied / Held / Stopped / Reverted), so a row still reads in greyscale. Monospace tabular timestamps; the action is one plain sentence with the number it wrote in it.

items.name: agent-trace-waterfall-01
items.title: Agent Trace — Where did the run spend its time, and where did it fail?
items.description: An execution waterfall for one multi-agent run: a stat strip where every number carries its comparison (duration vs p95, retries, tokens in/out, cost vs workflow average, failed at), the charts package’s Gantt at sub-second granularity with one row per agent span nested under its caller, and a context-flow chain that shows the hop where a required field was dropped.

items.name: finding-cards-01
items.title: Finding Cards — What did the copilot find?
items.description: Recoverable-spend findings as a row of cards: a status badge naming the kind, a one-line title, the recoverable figure as the only coloured number (kpi-sm), a two-sentence summary and a primary + secondary action, under a header that states the programme and the total the cards add up to. The primary action is what a person signs; the secondary always opens the evidence.

items.name: verdict-side-by-side-01
items.title: Verdict — Keep this, cancel that?
items.description: A keep-vs-cancel verdict side by side: two cards on the success/destructive washes with annual cost, a segmented seat-utilisation Meter and the deciding facts; a one-line reading of the comparison; “If you cancel” as four consequence stats; “How the copilot knows” as a numbered evidence list; and the refusal — the copilot prepares everything, a person signs.

items.name: handoff-inspector-01
items.title: Handoff Inspector — Where was the context dropped?
items.description: One edge of a multi-agent run: sender → a metric pill on the arrow (context size, latency, tokens, fields present of required) → receiver; a context-comparison table (sent vs expected, status badge per field) that shows the required field that was not sent; the payload size against the workflow baseline as a Meter with a marker; and the edge’s 24-hour health beside it.
